sections.h2: Which Buncombe County offices handle my tax bill?
sections.html:
One department, Tax Assessment, covers the whole cycle from its building at 182 College Street in Asheville. It is open weekdays from 8 am to 5 pm. The assessor lists, appraises and assesses property, while the collector bills and collects.

Each desk has its own number, so dial the one that fits your question.

  • Real estate values and appeal forms: 828-250-4940
  • Payments, balances and payment plans: 828-250-4910
  • Senior, disability and veteran relief: 828-250-4915
  • Business and personal property: 828-250-4930
  • Land records: 828-250-4970

Typing an address into tax.buncombenc.gov brings up the property record card, the bill and the appeal request. Print the record card before you list, so you can compare its details with the house. If you plan to sell, ask the collections desk for the balance on your parcel before you choose a closing date.

A law passed by the General Assembly in July 2026 makes the county hold off on its new values until January 1, 2027. Bills for 2026 therefore rest on the schedule from the 2021 reappraisal, even though the county had finished a reappraisal as of January 1, 2026 and mailed owners their new numbers.

Two measures were involved. S.B. 889 (S.L. 2026-8) delayed the schedule for a short list of counties that includes Buncombe. S.B. 474 (S.L. 2026-47) offered a way out through a revenue-neutral rate, which the county said would round to 40 cents. Commissioners chose to stay on the old values and a higher rate so the budget approved on June 2, 2026 would stand.

For most owners nothing moved. Unless you built or altered something, your value matches last year's, and last year's value already carried any Tropical Storm Helene adjustment. Mailed bills ran late, with most residential bills posted online first.

sections.h2: Rates on a 2026 Buncombe County bill
sections.html:
The county levy is 61.54 cents on each $100 of value, and the districts below add their own. Your parcel's address decides which of them apply.

2026 rates in Buncombe County
Taxing unitCents per $100 of value
Buncombe County61.54
Unified Fire District17.38
Asheville City Schools11.75

The county assigns values for every town and district inside it, so the delay reached those units too. The 40-cent option applied only to the county's own rate. City and town rates come from their own governing boards, so read the lines on your bill.

A bill is normally due September 1, and the county lets owners pay through the following January 5 without a penalty. For the 2026 bills, that final penalty-free day is January 5, 2027.

Once that date passes, state law charges 2% interest from January 6 through February 1, then three quarters of one percent per month or partial month. The postmark date is the payment date for anything mailed.

If you need more time, Tax Collections offers a Casual Payment Plan or a Preauthorized Debit Payment Plan. Enrolled owners are not subject to wage or bank account garnishment. Call 828-250-4910 and ask for a collection specialist.

sections.h2: How to contest your Buncombe County value
sections.html:
There are two routes: an informal review by Property Assessment, or a formal hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review. An appeal of the value on the current bill can be filed through December 31, 2026.

To start online, enter your address at tax.buncombenc.gov, pick View Parcel, then Tax Appeal Request. A mailed form is available from 828-250-4940. Over 16,000 appeals came in on the 2026 reappraisal values, and the county is holding the unresolved ones for the 2027 reappraisal, so nobody has to refile unless a decision came back and they disagree.

  • Under G.S. 105-322 the board may lower, raise or confirm a value after hearing evidence.
  • Ask for the hearing before the board adjourns; a decision notice mailed late gives you 15 days from its mailing.
  • The board mails its ruling within a month of adjourning.
  • Beyond that, notify the Property Tax Commission in writing within 30 days of the mailed ruling.

Buncombe administers the three programs set up by state law. Applications are open from January 1 through June 1, and a household can use only one program at a time.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: for owners aged 65 and up, or totally and permanently disabled, whose income is at or below the cap ($38,800 for 2026). It protects $25,000 or half the home's appraised value, whichever is larger.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value is removed, and no age or income test applies.
  • Circuit breaker: tax is limited to 4% of income, or 5% when income is over the cap but no higher than $58,200 for 2026. Whatever exceeds the limit is deferred, liened, and due when the owner sells or leaves.

The county warns that online videos describe a federal senior property tax exemption that does not exist, and it asks older owners to use only its official applications. Its General Assistance Program, described at buncombenc.gov/gap, offers short-term help with housing and utility costs.

The debt follows the parcel, so it is paid from the proceeds at or before closing. By state law the lien attaches on the date property is listed each year, with penalties, interest and costs added. The county can enforce it by filing a foreclosure suit where the land is located.

Call Tax Collections at 828-250-4910 for the payoff figure before fixing a closing date, and share it with your closing attorney so it is built into the settlement statement. If you hold a circuit breaker deferral, expect that balance to come due on the sale. A buyer's attorney will also want proof that the account is paid before the deed goes to the register of deeds at 205 College Street.

Owners with an open appeal should keep the paperwork handy, since the outcome applies to the 2027 value that the next buyer will see.

Buncombe's July 2025 population estimate was 277,417 in 142,799 housing units. The median owner-occupied home is $391,800, and 66.2% of homes are owned. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,785 a month, owners without one pay $505, and renters pay a median $1,362 in gross rent. Residents aged 65 or older make up 23.2%, and many in that group may qualify for the state relief programs above.

faqs.q: What rate does Buncombe County charge on 2026 bills?
faqs.a: The county levy is 61.54 cents per $100 of value on the 2021 schedule. Unified Fire District property adds 17.38 cents, and Asheville City Schools adds 11.75 cents.

faqs.q: When do Buncombe bills have to be paid?
faqs.a: September 1 is the usual due date, and no penalty applies through January 5 of the next year. Interest begins January 6.

faqs.q: Can I still protest my Buncombe County value?
faqs.a: Appeals of the current bill can be filed through December 31, 2026, at tax.buncombenc.gov or through 828-250-4940. Appeals already made on the 2026 values stay on hold for 2027.

faqs.q: Why is my 2026 Buncombe value unchanged?
faqs.a: A state law pushed the new reappraisal to 2027, so bills use the 2021 values. A change only shows up if you added or altered improvements.

faqs.q: Which Buncombe homeowners qualify for tax relief?
faqs.a: People 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled within the income cap, plus owners with a permanent and total service-connected disability. Applications run January 1 through June 1, and the exemptions desk is at 828-250-4915.
